title: Simulation foundations
description: Understand the evidence behind a virtual portfolio.

lessons.title: Virtual capital and costs
paragraphs: InvestIQ portfolios use virtual capital. Submitting a portfolio does not place an exchange order or transfer real money.
A simulated fee reduces residual cash once for the accepted portfolio. Valuation adds the value of whole-share holdings and residual cash; it does not deduct that fee again.

questions.prompt: What happens when you submit an InvestIQ portfolio?
options: A real exchange order is sent
questions.explanation: The simulation records a virtual portfolio; it does not send real orders.

questions.prompt: Where is the initial simulated fee reflected?
questions.explanation: The fee is included once by reducing residual cash at submission.

lessons.title: Whole shares and residual cash
paragraphs: Percentage targets are converted to whole shares using the documented submission price and fee reserve. Rounding down can leave uninvested virtual cash.
Target weights and achieved weights can differ. Review the server calculation before confirming. Cash remains part of total portfolio value.

questions.prompt: Can rounding down leave residual cash?
questions.explanation: Whole shares may cost less than a percentage target, leaving cash.

questions.prompt: Does residual cash count toward total portfolio value?
questions.explanation: Total value includes both holdings and residual cash.

lessons.title: Published closes and benchmarks
paragraphs: A valuation snapshot uses a common published session close. A missing or stale price is a limitation, not permission to invent a replacement price.

Portfolio return includes simulated costs. Benchmark return compares the benchmark close with its frozen baseline. Excess return is the difference between those percentage returns, expressed in percentage points.

questions.prompt: What should happen when a required closing price is missing?
questions.explanation: Missing evidence blocks a complete valuation.

questions.prompt: Portfolio return is 4% and benchmark return is 3%. What is excess return?
questions.explanation: Subtract benchmark return from portfolio return: 4 minus 3 equals 1 percentage point.

title: Reading portfolio metrics
description: Interpret simulation metrics and their limits.

lessons.title: Concentration and sector counts
paragraphs: The largest-position metric describes how much of total portfolio value sits in one holding. A sector count describes how many sector labels are present.

These are descriptive measures. A larger sector count alone cannot establish that a portfolio is safe, and several holdings can still move together. InvestIQ equity HHI excludes cash and sums squared equity-value weights.

questions.prompt: Does a larger sector count by itself prove a portfolio is safe?
questions.explanation: Sector count is a description, not a guarantee of safety.

questions.prompt: What does this simulation equity HHI exclude?
questions.explanation: Equity HHI normalizes weights over equity holdings and excludes cash.

lessons.title: Daily-close drawdown
paragraphs: Drawdown measures a decline from an earlier peak. InvestIQ records the largest decline across the initial virtual capital and available daily-close valuations.
Daily-close drawdown does not measure every intraday movement. A zero daily-close drawdown does not establish that prices never fell during the day.

questions.prompt: Drawdown compares a value with what?
questions.explanation: Drawdown is measured relative to an earlier peak.

questions.prompt: Do daily closes reveal every intraday decline?
questions.explanation: Prices between daily closes are not represented in daily-close snapshots.

lessons.title: Interpreting contributions
paragraphs: A holding contribution compares its current value with its original notional value. Holding price contributions exclude the portfolio-level simulated fee.

Use the recorded submission and price evidence to describe results. A locked portfolio without trades cannot support a claim that its owner sold too early. Outcomes alone do not reveal a learner’s intentions.

questions.prompt: Do individual holding price contributions include the portfolio-level fee?
questions.explanation: The single fee is accounted for at portfolio level.

questions.prompt: Can a locked portfolio with no trades prove that someone sold too early?
questions.explanation: Without a sale in the evidence, this claim is unsupported.
